extracted.intended_audience: surgeons, physicians, medical researchers, and Royal Society readers
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and reporting of incidence, mortality, recurrence, and possible causes of urinary calculi using hospital registers, operative series, and regional population denominators; includes surgical outcomes and recommendations for observation and technique. Also includes measurement/observation practices for magnetic dip observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement apparatus and procedure for dip observations
rubrics_metrics.description: The circle is of six inches diameter only, being made so small for greater portability: except in size, the whole apparatus is in all respects similar to the one with which the observations already detailed were made. The agate supports are levelled in the same manner by a circular plate carrying a level, and the mode of observation was the same in every particular. The needle was fitted with a screw and weights, on Professor Meyer’s plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure instrument portability without changing other construction; level agate supports with a circular plate and use consistent observation mode; fit needle with screw and weights per Meyer to standardize readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument/observer and needle-type comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Several series are reported by instrument size and observer: 'Instrument of 12 inches diameter. Observer, Captain Sabine.' 'Instrument of 6 inches diameter. Observer, Mr. Douglas.' Results are also grouped by needle type (common needle, Meyer’s needle, adjustable axis, Mr. Dollond’s needle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report who observed, instrument dimensions, and needle type; compare series across these factors to detect systematic differences attributable to instrument or observer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation and averaging of repeated observations
rubrics_metrics.description: The several results ... being collected in one view ... Mean ... Whence the final result of the dip ... is 69°47' North.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect multiple experiment results, present them grouped by relevant factors (instrument, needle, observer), and compute means to produce a final reported result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal trend analysis of magnetic dip
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of observations in 1821 and 1828 shows a diminution of 17'.5 in seven years, or 2'.5 per year. Comparison with Paris series (1798–1828) and splitting intervals gives different annual rates (e.g., 4'.93 per year for first portion, 2'.75 for second).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare contemporaneous and historical series, split long intervals to examine changes in rate over time, and compute annual rates to assess temporal trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for repeated/frequent observations (dip)
rubrics_metrics.description: A repetition of the observations in London at the expiration of another seven years, and a continuation of those at Paris, will probably show decisively whether the annual change in the amount of the dip ... is diminishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan periodic, repeated observations at the same sites to determine whether apparent changes are persistent trends or artefacts; increase frequency when small changes are suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of hospital registers to estimate incidence
rubrics_metrics.description: From the establishment of the Norfolk and Norwich Hospital in 1772 ... 649 operations of lithotomy have been performed in it ... If we deduct ... cases which have come from Suffolk and Cambridgeshire ... there will remain 575 furnished by the population of the county of Norfolk, which amounts to 351,000; and this will produce about 10.26 cases per annum, or 1 for every 34,000 inhabitants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use long-term hospital registers and local census/population denominators to calculate annual incidence and per-capita rates; exclude or adjust for cases referred from outside the target population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment for referrals and hospital catchment bias
rubrics_metrics.description: The hospital contains about 100 patients ... If we put aside ... the cases occurring in the Norfolk district ... we shall then have 1 calculous case for every 118,000 inhabitants. ... Bristol, owing to its central position, receives patients from the counties of Somerset, Gloucester, Wilts, and Monmouth, as well as from South Wales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for hospitals' catchment areas and referral patterns when attributing cases to geographic populations; be cautious comparing institutions with differing referral inflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and subregional stratification
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerable differences exist with regard to the ratio of numbers furnished by the different hundreds of Norfolk; the eastern parts of the county, however, contributing more largely than the western. Examples of anomalies (e.g., Chippenham) are noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze incidence by fine-grained geographic subdivisions (hundreds, towns) to detect local hotspots or anomalies, and report those contrasts explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age stratification of incidence and mortality
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables exhibit the number of operations with mortality at different periods of life: e.g., under 14: mortality 1 in 14.6; 14 and upwards: 1 in 5.17; 14–40: 1 in 10.33; 40 and upwards: 1 in 3.74. Detailed age bands (inf. to 10, 10–14, 14–20, etc.) are provided with operations, cured, died, mortality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stratify cases and outcomes by age bands when reporting surgical outcomes; present counts and derived mortality ratios for each age group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sex differences and sex-specific treatment effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of female cases in the whole has been 31; the proportion, 1 in 20, and the deaths 1 in 15.5. But from the improved practice by dilatation, all risk of life, in the abstraction of calculi from females, seems to be taken away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sex-specific incidence and mortality; note when different surgical approaches (e.g., dilatation in females) alter risk profiles and prognosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stone size (weight) association with operative mortality
rubrics_metrics.description: The operation of lithotomy is always attended with more danger, when calculi are large ... of 52 cases of adult males in which calculi of 2 oz. or more occurred, 31 died, or nearly 2 in 3; while in 282 cases with stones <2 oz. the mortality only amounted to 37, or rather less than 1 in 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stratify outcomes by stone size (weight); recognize larger calculi as a major prognostic factor and consider mechanical means (Earle's method, Civiale's lithotrity) to reduce stone magnitude as alternatives to high-risk extraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator skill and technique influence on outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Two distinguished lithotomists had differing mortalities across early and later series; use of blunt gorget and other technical choices are linked to success. 'Mr. Martineau dated his principal success from the time that he employed the blunt gorget, according to Cheselden’s method.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report operator identity/experience and the surgical technique used; assess how technique changes and surgeon skill over time affect mortality and success rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recurrence frequency and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recurrences of stone seem to be not very frequent; 14 instances, or 1 in 46 only, being found ... The production of the second calculus took place, in 4 of these cases, within 1 year; in 5, within 2 years; in 3, within 3 years; while in the 2 remaining cases ... after 7 and 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report recurrence counts and the interval distribution between primary and repeat operations to characterize relapse risk and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familial and occupational predisposition (data limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: A constitutional predisposition to the occurrence of calculous diseases, unquestionably exists in certain families. ... On the comparative infrequency among sea-faring people is discussed, but the Norwich register did not record occupations until late years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and report family histories and occupations as potential risk factors but acknowledge register incompleteness; avoid strong causal claims where occupation/family data are lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dietary/environmental hypotheses with caution
rubrics_metrics.description: The large employment of ill fermented farinaceous food, which marks ... the commonalty of Norfolk, may perhaps be regarded as favouring the occurrence of calculous diseases; but a much coarser ... material ... has been ... used in Scotland and the North of England, without being productive of such an effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose dietary or environmental factors as hypotheses but test against counterexamples and multiple regions; do not attribute causation without sufficient comparative evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and convention for mortality reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Norfolk and Norwich Hospital, it is the invariable practice, for no case to be put down as a recovery from the stone operation, if the patient die in the hospital, of any disease which may even have come on during his convalescence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state counting conventions (e.g., whether deaths during convalescence count as operation failures) because such conventions materially affect reported mortality rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-quality caveats and register completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: It is exceedingly difficult, from the want of efficient registers, to procure such data as can connect the occurrence of a certain number of cases with a certain known population. ... the register of the Norfolk and Norwich Hospital does not afford any evidence on occupations, as it is only of late years that the occupations of patients have been inserted in it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly declare limitations of registers (missing fields, incomplete coverage, late additions) and qualify incidence/mortality estimates accordingly.
